headline: Last session: Sensex gained 308 points as Nifty reclaimed 23,000 level ahead of weekend

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 2 November.

why: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) turned net buyers in the final week of October despite pulling out Rs 34,843 crore during the month.
Net GST collection surged past Rs 2.03 lakh crore in October, reflecting strong domestic economic activity.
Major oil marketing companies reported strong Q2 combined profits of Rs 30,106 crore.
UPI daily average transaction values exceeded ₹1 trillion in October, reinforcing consumer spending momentum.
whatHappening: On the last trading day (October 30), Nifty reclaimed the 23,000 level while Sensex ended 308 points higher.
Hyundai Motor recorded its highest-ever sales for October, driven by strong export demand.
Oil refining and marketing PSUs IOC, BPCL, and HPCL reported robust quarterly earnings accounting for nearly 39% of last year's annual earnings.
Market participants are looking ahead to the November 2-6 trading week for further directional cues.
summary:
On the last trading session, Indian benchmark indices closed higher with Nifty reclaiming 23,000 and Sensex adding 308 points.
Strong macroeconomic indicators such as record October GST mop-up and UPI transactions provided underlying support.
The stock market is closed today due to the weekend and will reopen for regular trading on Monday, 2 November.
